newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs end on high note after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs end on high note after U.S. data.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds jumped on the bandwagon to close higher with U.S. Treasuries and Bunds on Thursday after news that the October U.S. trade gap shrunk more than expected, traders said.
The Bundesbank's decision to leave interest rates unchanged had no impact on the market and would contribute to keeping the market steady in the year-end, one said.

The benchmark 2006 OLO closed at a yield of 5.94 percent compared with the close of 5.96 the day before. The 10-year OLO/Bund yield spread rose to 11 basis points from nine but traders said it would stay around 10 for the rest of the year.
Traders said that U.S. Treasuries were currently calling all the shots in a market which was almost exclusively professional.
"We see some window-dressing, traders cleaning up their books, some position shuffling," said Geert Huyghe at CERA Bank.
Traders were now looking at U.S. GDP data on Friday but did not believe they could rattle the market.
They said that although the Treasury market looked weak from a technical point of view, the strength of short-term interest rates was reassuring the market.
